title: TDMA latch single-threaded guarantee exceeds code; document contract or take seq_lock
description: link_ctx.h:94-96 'latch pair guarantees at most one lichen_tdma_init per (context,epoch)' but tx.c:70-74 mutates latch/tdma without seq_lock while load_key/set_epoch/cleanup touch ctx->epoch under lock. Idempotent+fail-open racy writes, no worse than HEAD statics, but doc overpromises. Either document single-thread-per-context contract or serialize.
close_reason: link_ctx.h TDMA latch doc extended in place (doc-only; chose document-over-serialize since the racy window is idempotent and fail-open and nxwa offers either remedy): latch guarantee now explicitly holds per single-threaded context owner; the latch is checked/updated by lichen_link_tx() outside seq_lock, so concurrent TX vs lichen_link_load_key()/cleanup() on the SAME context is caller-error (cross-referenced lichen_link_cleanup() thread-safety warning, matching surrounding doc style); worst-case racy outcomes stated as a redundant lichen_tdma_init() or one ungated TX (fail-open, matching HEAD statics), not serialized. No code change; latch logic untouched. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra exit 0 on link_ctx.c and tdma.c consuming the header.
